subject: Post-demo: engine trio selection, benchmarks & ops guardrails
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@horizonhealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: recommended engine trio, bench links & next steps

Thanks again for the time today, Olivia — really helpful to see the demo flow and the example escalation cases. Recap below plus a recommended shortlist (three engines) that balance Horizon's requirements across latency, cost, and hallucination risk. I included quick numbers from our lab runs and attached the full CSV + prompt-set bundle.

Summary of what we heard
- Primary goal: <10% user friction on triage flows; P95 latency target ~350ms for short-turn interactions (100–256 tokens).
- Quality sensitivity: high for diagnosis summaries (low hallucination tolerance).
- Budget: constrained — target to keep per-1k-token inference cost under $2 in pilot.

Recommended engine trio (prioritized)
1) Redwood-lite-8q (low-latency): P95 ~220ms (single-token windows), best for quick triage buttons and multi-turn routing. Cost: lowest. Quality: good for structured extraction, weaker on narrative summarization.
2) Redwood-balanced-16q (quantized medium): P95 ~380ms, best overall balance — good factuality, smaller hallucination rate in our medical prompts, moderate cost. Good default for your summary/triage mix.
3) Redwood-clarion-1 (high-fidelity): P95 ~720ms, higher cost but meaningfully better F1/precision on subjective summarization tasks. Recommend for final report generation and legal-facing outputs.

Key tradeoffs and mitigations
- Latency vs quality: we suggest routing short interactive requests to lite-8q and heavier summarization to clarion-1 with an autoscale rule.
- Cost control: prefix caching + prompt templates reduce repeat token spend; we've flagged opportunities in the attached prompt set.
- Regression guardrails: include small eval sets (we've added a 120-sample regression pack in the Drive link) to catch quality drops across model swaps.

Asks / next steps
- Can you share a 2k sample of live prompts/logs (anonymized) so we can run a targeted bench? (we can sign a narrow NDA).
- Confirm whether P95 350ms is a hard SLO for the pilot or an aspirational target.
- Proposed next call: Tue 5/25 or Wed 5/26 — 30 minutes to review bench results and pilot scope.

Attachments (zipped): hh-benchmarks-20270524.csv, hh-prompt-sets-v1.zip, pilot-scope-matrix.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll schedule a follow-up once I hear preferred slots.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Tessa — great summary and useful breakdown. A few quick questions: 

- For the P95s you quoted, are those measurements from our expected token lengths (mostly 50–300 tokens) or mixed? We are particularly worried about P95 for the interactive triage UI.
- For hallucination risk: do you have example failure modes for the balanced engine on clinical narratives? We need to understand the tradeoffs before routing anything to a high-cost model.

We can share a 2k-anonymized prompt sample — procurement will handle the data agreement. I’m available Tue 5/25 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 5/26 after 13:00 PT.

Olivia Grant

olivia@horizonhealth.ai

Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: recommended engine trio, bench links & next steps

Flagging a couple of commercial/ops points for the pilot:
- Pricing: for a 6-week pilot (expected ~5M tokens across users) we can offer a pilot commitment price to get effective per-1k cost closer to $1.70 (DEAL-5869). Need to confirm token estimate with Horizon once they share sample traffic.
- Capacity: if they route many concurrent short interactions we should reserve 2x lite-8q slots to hit P95 safety; capacity reservation would be part of the pilot SOW.
- Legal/Procurement: Marissa — please prepare a short SOW + narrow DPA (we'll request anonymized logs only).

I'll stand by for the scheduled follow-up. Happy to join to discuss commercial guardrails.

-Ben
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks Olivia. Tue 5/25 10:00 PT works for us; I booked 30 minutes and sent a calendar invite. Agenda: 1) confirm P95 target and sample prompt shape, 2) review the attached bench CSV highlights, 3) align on pilot scope and SOW timeline.

Quick answers while we prep:
- Bench P95s above are for 50–300 token windows (we partitioned runs to match the triage/summarization split). The full CSV has the P50/P95/P99 slices by token length.
- Failure modes for the balanced engine: a) occasional entity confabulation in long clinical narratives (>600 tokens), b) low-confidence hallucination on ambiguous lab result descriptions. Mitigations: constrained decoding + entity-preserving templates, plus pre/post-validation step using deterministic extraction model. Ben and I drafted a short regression pack for those cases in the Drive link.

Please upload the anonymized sample to this secure folder: https://drive.google.com/secure-upload/horizon-sample (we can accept S3 link as well). Once we have the sample, Ben will run a targeted bench and share an annotated results sheet within 48 hours.

Attachments included in this thread: hh-benchmarks-20270524.csv (summary), hh-prompt-sets-v1.zip (annotated templates), pilot-scope-matrix.xlsx (commercial + ops checklist)

Looking forward to the call — I’ll loop in Legal/Procurement if we need to accelerate the SOW.

Best,
Tessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
